text:
The change adds a module logger to `app/weather.py` and logs every forecast request at INFO level. It also adds a test that checks the request gets logged.

**Problem 1: the API key is written to the logs (R1, blocking).** In `forecast`, the URL is built with `urlencode({'city': city, 'key': self._api_key})`. The new line `log.info("forecast request: %s", url)` then logs that full URL, so every forecast call writes `key=<api key>` in plain text to whatever handlers are set up. Log files, log shippers and anyone who can read the logs would get the key. R1 says: "Never log a secret: an API key, a token or a password." Only the city should be logged.

**Problem 2: the new test hides the leak instead of catching it (should_fix).** `test_forecast_logs_its_request` only checks that `"city=Lyon"` is in `caplog.text`. Its captured log actually contains `key=fake-key-0000`, and the test still passes. It should also check that the key is absent, so the leak can't come back.

```json

  "findings": [
    {
      "path": "app/weather.py",
      "side": "head",
      "line": 20,
      "end_line": 20,
      "line_text": "        log.info(\"forecast request: %s\", url)",
      "severity": "blocking",
      "category": "repo_rule",
      "title": "Logged request URL contains the API key in its `key` query parameter",
      "body": "When forecast() runs with INFO logging on, the full URL is logged, and it includes `key=<api_key>` from urlencode. So the secret API key is written to every log handler and to anything that ships or stores logs.",
      "defect_key": "secret_logged",
      "suggestion": "        log.info(\"forecast request: city=%s\", city)",
      "pre_existing": false,
      "rule": "R1"
    },
    {
      "path": "tests/test_weather.py",
      "side": "head",
      "line": 15,
      "end_line": 15,
      "line_text": "    assert \"city=Lyon\" in caplog.text",
      "severity": "should_fix",
      "category": "tests",
      "title": "Logging test does not check that the API key is kept out of the log",
      "body": "The test only checks that the city appears in the log. The captured text also contains `key=fake-key-0000`, and the test passes anyway, so it hides the secret leak instead of catching it.",
      "defect_key": "missing_secret_absence_assertion",
      "suggestion": "    assert \"city=Lyon\" in caplog.text\n    assert \"fake-key-0000\" not in caplog.text",
      "pre_existing": false,
      "rule": null
    }
  ],
```
